Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

RFRed Fox9m ago

Lead with the recommendation; the finding can follow.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

MLMaya Lindqvist3m ago

Was it twice? The log says once, on the 14th.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

RFRed Foxjust now

Walkers need a sign here before the meadow is gone.

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To tell people something about the content right next to it: a problem to fix, a result, a caution, a useful fact.
  • After an action, in place, to say what happened when it is not obvious ("Copied to the clipboard" is obvious; "Project created in ../field-notes" is not).

When not to use

  • For a single field's error: use the error line of cmp-text-field, cmp-select or cmp-checkbox.
  • For a state label on an item: use cmp-status-pill.
  • For marketing emphasis or decoration: inline alerts are for information people act on.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • info — a useful fact or a next step, with no problem: blue.
  • success — something worked, and what it produced: green.
  • warning — something will go wrong or is incomplete unless people act: amber.
  • error — something failed or blocks progress, and how to fix it: red. Announced at once.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-inline-alert ds-inline-alert--<tone>" role="status">, or role="alert" for the error tone.
  • Icon: <span class="ds-icon" data-icon="<name>"></span> first: alert for warning and error, check for success, info for info.
  • Body: <div class="ds-inline-alert__body"> holding an optional <p class="ds-inline-alert__title"> (a few words, strong) and <p class="ds-inline-alert__text"> (one or two sentences).
  • Any action (a button or link) sits outside the alert, after it, in the screen's layout.

Accessibility

  • role="status" for info, success and warning, so the message is read politely; role="alert" for errors, so it is read at once. Add the role to an alert that appears after the page loads; an alert present from the start may omit it.
  • The tone is told by the icon and the words as well as the colour; titles say "Error", "Done" and so on where the text alone would not.
  • Text uses the tone's text colour on the tone's surface, which meets AA in every theme.
  • Never move focus to an alert, except an error summary after a failed submit.

Interaction

  • Not interactive itself. It appears in place without pushing focus anywhere, and does not slide or fade in for show (int-02, int-04).
  • When the problem is fixed, it is removed or replaced by the success tone at once (int-06).
  • A message arrives and leaves with a fade over --ds-motion-settle (data-ds-arriving for one frame, data-ds-leaving until hidden); the alert itself never moves.

Content rules

  • Lead with what matters: what happened or what to do. "Choose another folder name, or add --force to overwrite it."
  • Title (optional): two to five words, no full stop: "Folder already exists".
  • Text: one or two plain sentences; name the thing and the fix. No blame, no "Oops".
  • Commands and paths in code style are fine inside the text.

Do and don't

  • Do put the alert next to the thing it is about, above any action that fixes it.
  • Do show one alert per problem; combine related messages into one.
  • Don't stack several alerts of different tones in one place.
  • Don't use the error tone for warnings; reserve red for things that failed.
